newVerdicts.evidence: tasks.py:113/118 — regex is unanchored (search, no host/path anchor), so the factual observation is true. But tasks.py:1140-1147 uses the parsed repository solely as a team-scoped lookup key (for_team(team_id), provider="github", repository__iexact, enabled=True, connected_by_user_id set, installation_id non-blank); a miss returns at 1151-1153. tasks.py:1159 — the URL is never fetched; the GitHub call uses repo_config.repository (canonical) and repo_config.installation_id, so only pr_number (\d+, int-safe) comes from the parsed string — no SSRF/redirect surface. team_id is an explicit task arg (1111), not URL-derived. A lookalike-host URL parses to the identical (owner/repo, N) a well-formed github.com URL would, so the proposed host/path anchoring prevents nothing an influencer of pr_url couldn't do with a valid URL; the residual arbitrary-pr_number concern is not closed by the suggested fix and is covered by finding M9.

newVerdicts.evidence: The flag's sole producer is products/stamphog/backend/temporal/activities.py:451 (`self_driving_review=bool(output.get("inbox_review"))`), passed through the bool-typed parameter of build_reviewer_invocation (products/stamphog/backend/logic/reviewer.py:101) into the context dict (line 131) and serialized via json.dumps (line 137). Pure defensive-coding speculation against an unreachable input.

newVerdicts.evidence: tasks.py:1109 does set max_retries=3/delay=5, but every failure branch logs (logger.exception at 1149, 1164; logger.warning at 1161) and retry exhaustion raises MaxRetriesExceededError — loss is not silent. newVerdicts.evidence: receivers.py:75-79 docstring documents re-fires on unchanged targets as deliberate with bounded cost ("a same-head re-trigger costs one fetch (early-exit)"). No hot-path, unbounded, or N+1 defect introduced.

newVerdicts.evidence: receivers.py (pr75215_tree): handle_task_run_saved registers _start_review then _start_stamphog_review via transaction.on_commit without robust=True; _start_review's deferred imports of products.review_hog.backend.temporal.client/.types are outside its try block (only start_review_pr_workflow is wrapped). Django 5.2 run_and_clear_commit_hooks (source verified): a non-robust callback that raises drops all remaining popped callbacks and propagates into the committer. So an import failure in _start_review would suppress the stamphog dispatch and raise into the tasks commit path.
newVerdicts.notes: Mechanism is technically accurate, but the only propagating trigger is the product's own temporal package being unimportable — a process-wide systemic deploy breakage (monorepo single env, sys.modules-cached after first success), under which every ReviewHog inbox review is already dead; the incremental harm is only suppressing the stamphog leg for dual-toggle users. robust=True (or imports inside the try) is cheap, reasonable hardening, but this is defensive robustness against a practically unreachable edge, not a production defect this PR introduces.

newVerdicts.evidence: webhooks.py:68-77 branch leg has no terminal-status/deleted filter and no order_by (arbitrary .first() on collision); wizard leg (84-96) does exclude both, proving the omission is leg-specific. facade/api.py:501-510 (new in diff) reuses that leg as positive self-driving identification for the stamphog carve-out. Refutation's base-branch premise only covers auto_start.py:253 runs, which are internal=True (line 263) and rejected at api.py:508; the matchable non-internal shape stores the head branch in `branch` per the PR's own tests (_make_run(branch="posthog-code/sd-fix") matched via head_branch). Carve-out gates (bot author, repo-native head, enabled config, team match, opted-in reviewer) bound impact to stale-provenance stamphog review within the same team/repo.
newVerdicts.notes: The staleness hazard is real (branch leg can return a completed/deleted-task run, unordered), but exploitation needs a same-team same-repo bot PR whose head ref collides with an old run's stored head branch plus pr_url-binding failure; worst case is wrong-report attribution, not a security issue. The suggested fix (exclude terminal runs) would regress legitimate post-completion identification; prefer-non-terminal ordering is the right shape. Downgraded from should_fix to consider.

newVerdicts.evidence: tasks.py:1109-1245 — process_inbox_pr_review has no bot/fork/run re-verification and stamps inbox_review (1176-1181, 1229), which bypasses gates (tasks.py:881, 944, 968; activities.py:451 self_driving_review). However: sole caller is review_hog's in-process receiver (receivers.py:225 via facade api.py:149) which already gates task.signal_report_id (receivers.py:98), not task.internal (:104), and an opted-in resolved reviewer (:111-126) — the queued values ARE the triggering run's own identity, unforgeable by any external caller. output.pr_url is written only by the trusted agent server or the fork-safe webhook backstop (webhooks.py:178-185: head repo must equal base repo, fills only an unset pr_url). process_inbox_pr_review additionally requires a team-scoped synced+enabled repo config (tasks.py:1140-1147). newVerdicts.notes: The finding's code observations are accurate but its threat model conflates the webhook leg (untrusted arbitrary PR events, hence positive identification in _inbox_rereview_carve_out) with the receiver leg (trusted in-process run save reusing the run's own recorded PR URL). Re-verifying the queued run/report IDs guards nothing. The only residual value is defense-in-depth: adding _is_bot_authored + head-repo==base checks on the fetched PR in process_inbox_pr_review would mirror the webhook carve-out cheaply — a consider-level hardening improvement, not a must_fix security defect.

The engine-side gap (_attach_familiarity has no self_driving check) is only exploitable by a hypothetical future caller that sets self_driving_review while also injecting PR numbers — a defense-in-depth suggestion, not a defect introduced by this PR. The docstring "familiarity is deliberately absent" is accurate as shipped.

newVerdicts.evidence: receivers.py:224-234 does catch and log queue_inbox_pr_review failures (mechanism confirmed), and the stamphog webhook carve-out is later-deliveries-only (tasks.py:168-171: "the initial review is the receiver leg's job"). But permanent loss is refuted: the receiver fires on every TaskRun save touching output (receivers.py:85-89; docstring 77-79 "re-fire it deliberately"), process_inbox_pr_review's contract depends on exactly these re-fires with head-keyed dedupe (tasks.py:1124-1128), and re-fire sources exist: set_task_run_output saves output wholesale preserving pr_url (products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:2149-2154), pr_merged output writes (products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:276-292), plus any later push hits the synchronize carve-out. The swallow is a documented module invariant ("broker being down must never surface into the saver", receivers.py:213), runs in transaction.on_commit (receivers.py:131) where raising is useless, and mirrors the pre-existing _start_review Temporal leg (receivers.py:246,272-273).
newVerdicts.notes: Loss requires a compound rare scenario (broker down at the one dispatch + no later output save + no later head-changing delivery), and the consequence is one missed approve-first Stamphog review on an opt-in experimental flow still covered by ReviewHog and human review, with a full traceback logged. newVerdicts.evidence: pr75215_tree/products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1155-1162 — fetch precedes dedupe by design (dedupe keys on current head "which only GitHub knows"); rate-limit path retries with adaptive countdown. tasks.py:1202-1221 — head-keyed dedupe early-exits after one GET. products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:82-96 — receiver drops created saves and non-output declared-field saves; dispatch gated on non-internal signal-report task + resolved opted-in reviewer. receivers.py:76-79 — docstring documents the deliberate refire tradeoff ("a same-head re-trigger costs one fetch (early-exit)"). products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:2154,2163-2172 — output saves are a bounded handful per run (set_task_run_output, webhook backstop); log appends go to S3 without touching output, so they never fire the receiver.
newVerdicts.notes: The finding's mechanical facts are right (no coalescing cache, GET before dedupe) but its failure scenario is not: dispatches are bounded per run, not an "unbounded stream"; each redundant fire costs one read-only GET; the refire is a documented deliberate recovery mechanism for lost webhooks; rate-limit hits are absorbed by adaptive retry. A coalescing window is at most a low-value micro-optimization, not a defect.

judges.rationale: M1 dominates recall: 14 verified-real findings mapping to 14 distinct clusters (~67% of the ~21 real clusters the whole panel surfaced), including 5 solo-covered real issues no other model verified (X3 trusted-provenance rendering, X17 unindexed TaskRun.branch scan, P4 stale draft-on-purpose copy, P8 missing cross-leg head dedupe, P17 FAILED-run retry loop) plus sole real coverage of the unscoped find_task_run tenant check (P13). M2 is a clear second: 7 reals collapsing to 6 clusters (Y5/Q5 duplicate the dead internal=True carve-out), with 3 solo clusters (Y4 fail-soft ambiguity, Q12 retarget copy mismatch, Q19 false 'commits pushed' claim). M6 takes third on a tiebreak: its 6 reals cover only 4 clusters (J5/L3 and L4/L6 are intra-model dupes), the same cluster count as M4 and M5, but it has 2 solo-covered real clusters (J4 canonical-reviewer gate contradiction, L9 fire-and-forget dispatch) and more raw real findings. M5 and M4 are effectively tied at 4 reals / 4 clusters / 0 solo clusters each; M5 is ordered ahead marginally for covering the merge-blocking migration-0019 conflict (K6), but their scores are equal. M3 is last: only 3 reals (T6, T7, T10), every one redundantly covered by multiple other models, contributing zero unique real-issue coverage. Noise (e.g., M1's 30 non-real findings) was ignored per the lens definition.

M6 leads on precision: 6/16 = 37.5% verified-real, and its hits are dense in value (4 must_fix: J5, L3, L4, L6, plus J4, L9) — a reviewer reads 16 findings and gets 6 real ones, the best signal-to-noise on the panel, though its junk still includes the stale-checkout fabrication L5. M1 is second at 14/44 = 31.8%; the rate is respectable and includes must_fix P12, but the sheer volume (30 junk findings, including the self-undermining meta-finding P24 and low-value noise like P11/P22) taxes the reader more in absolute terms than any other model. M2 drops to 7/36 = 19.4% and its false positives are the worst kind — outright fabrications (Y16 misquoted regex, Y13 disproven Django on_commit semantics, Y15) and a false stale-tree claim (Q1) — which erode reviewer trust beyond what the raw rate shows. M3 is 3/17 = 17.6%; low volume did not buy accuracy — its entire R set produced zero verified reals, and it emitted the false tach.toml claim T1 and false max_migration claim R2. M5 (4/28 = 14.3%) and M4 (4/30 = 13.3%) sit at the bottom: M5's junk includes three stale-checkout/false-registration claims (M8, K9, K7), and M4 pairs the worst rate with zero must_fix among its 4 reals (U13, U14, V8, V9), meaning 26 of 30 findings were wasted reviewer time with no high-severity payoff. M5 edges M4 on both rate and having a must_fix hit (K6).

M6 wins on heavy-catch density: 4 verified must_fix from only 16 findings, covering the receiver-leg approval-redirect hole from both sides (L4 dispatch, L6 worker) and the semi-exclusive migration-leaf CI blocker in both runs (J5, L3 — shared only with M5's K6; four models missed a deterministic merge-queue failure). It also owns the only verified-real finding in two more clusters (J4 canonical-reviewer contract contradiction, L9 fire-and-forget dispatch loss). Its sole heavy miss is the dead internal=True carve-out leg. M2 is the only model with must_fix hits on both top security clusters — the dead carve-out leg in both runs (Y5, Q5) and the receiver-linkage hole (Q18, the single most thorough writeup of the approval-redirect blast radius) — plus should_fix Y8 (stale-approval dismissal blocking); but all three of its must_fix land in clusters 3-4 other models also hit, so it has no exclusivity premium. M1 has just 1 must_fix (P12, dead leg) and under-called the receiver hole as should_fix (X20), but its should_fix portfolio adds real unique impact: X3 (trusted provenance rendered solely off the flag) and P8 (webhook/receiver double-review gap) are verified-real nowhere else, plus unique-real P13/P17/P19. M3's tiny output (3 real) hits both top clusters at must_fix (T7, T10) but contributes nothing M2 didn't already cover and nothing unique. M5 gets credit for the rare migration catch (K6) and receiver cluster at should_fix (M9), but that's the whole impact story. M4 is last: 0 must_fix, no heavy cluster at heavy severity, and its receiver-cluster attempts failed verification — it missed everything that mattered most.
